e89b79: This week you review three classes: the basic prepositions a, de, en, con and sin; the contractions al and del; and adverbs of place, time and manner. You use them in Granada, Nicaragua, to get around the city and explain routes.
mv9v1i: A, en, de: going, being, coming
1wtktnl: **A** marks the **destination**, with verbs of movement like _ir_, _llegar_ or _venir_: _Voy **a** Granada_, _Llego **a** la estación_.
10fztpn: **En** marks the **place** where you are or do something, with no movement: _Estoy **en** Granada_, _Trabajo **en** una tienda_. With transport you also use **en**: _en bus_, _en barco_ (but _a pie_).
1nhj9dj: **De** marks **origin** (_Vengo **de** Masaya_, _Soy **de** León_) and also the **owner**: _la casa **de** Inés_.
1m2b02c: The question tells you the preposition
eac6it: **Con** tells you the **company** or what you carry: _Paseo **con** mi hermana_, _un café **con** leche_, _una casa **con** jardín_.
lewxs6: **Sin** tells you what there **isn't** or what you don't carry: _un jugo **sin** azúcar_, _Salgo **sin** paraguas_. Usually you don't put an article after **sin**: _sin dinero_, _sin prisa_.
13a38lv: The five prepositions go **before** the noun or the place. And in questions, they also go first: _¿**Con** quién vas?_, _¿**De** dónde eres?_
nb7jjo: Al and del: only with el
1exier4: When **a** or **de** come before the article **el**, they join into one word: **a + el = al**, **de + el = del**. _Voy **al** mercado_, _Vengo **del** parque_.
1y5iw3l: It only happens with **el**. With _la_, _los_ and _las_ there's no contraction: _a la iglesia_, _de los barcos_, _a las islas_. Nor with other prepositions: _en el lago_, _con el guía_.
15jl8dj: With **él** (pronoun, with an accent) they don't join: _Este regalo es **de él**_. And to explain a route, you use **de… a…** with its contractions: _**del** hotel **al** lago_.
ifgvj3: Adverbs never change: they have no masculine or plural forms. **Where**: _aquí_ (near me), _ahí_ (near you), _allí_ (far), _cerca_, _lejos_. **When**: _hoy_, _mañana_, _ahora_, _temprano_, _tarde_, and to put things in order: _primero_, _después_, _luego_. **How**: _bien_, _mal_, _despacio_, _rápido_.
dmdvb0: **Muy** goes before an **adjective** or another **adverb**: _muy bonito_, _muy cerca_, _muy bien_. **Mucho** goes with a **verb** (_Caminas **mucho**_) or with a **noun**, and then it agrees: _**mucho** calor_, _**muchas** iglesias_.
ozjcn8: Careful: **después** on its own, at the end or between two actions (_Primero comemos y **después** paseamos_); **después de** + a noun (_después del almuerzo_).
i7ck8u: Look at the word next to it: is it an adjective or an adverb? **Muy**. Is it a verb or a thing? **Mucho**.
15d1nz2: Before an adjective: **muy**, which doesn't change.

ekzwz9: **Al** and **del** are a single syllable and join the next word: _al-mer-ca-do_, _del-par-que_. If you hear _a la_ or _de la_, that's two syllables: _a-la-pla-za_. That extra syllable tells you the word is feminine.
1vzly2t: A **d** between vowels or after a vowel is **soft**: the tongue lightly touches the teeth, without force, like _th_ in English _this_. It happens in _de_, _del_, _todo_, _mercado_, _a dónde_.
1mcq79j: At the start of a sentence or after **n** or **l**, the d is stronger: _¿**D**ónde estás?_, _cuan**d**o_, _el **d**ía_.
ocu2sj: **Al** and **del** are always written as one word: never _a el_ or _de el_ (except with the pronoun _él_, with an accent). On the other hand, **a la**, **de la**, **a los**, **de las** are always written separately.
